name: Apple
title: How Apple makes money, live: revenue, profit and where it goes
description: Apple's $416.2B year as a live clock: iPhone, Mac, iPad and Services revenue, where the money goes, buybacks and dividends, per employee and by region. From the FY2025 10-K.
tagline: The iPhone is half of sales, but Services is 26% of revenue and 42% of gross profit.
as_of: Fiscal year ended Sep 27, 2025 (10-K filed Oct 31, 2025)

10k: Apple Inc., Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended Sep 27, 2025 (filed Oct 31, 2025)
facts: SEC EDGAR XBRL companyfacts, Apple Inc. (CIK 0000320193): annual revenue and net income from each year's 10-K

blocks.label: projected from annual 10-K averages
blocks.note: Each counter = FY2025 total from the 10-K ÷ 31,449,600 seconds (364 days, the 52-week fiscal year). These are averages, not real-time sales. Buybacks and dividends are the cash paid in the cash flow statement. [[10k]]

sections.title: Money in, money out
sections.lede: Every dollar of FY2025 revenue, from where it came to where it went. Values in US$ billions.

blocks.title: Income statement, FY2025
blocks.note: US$ millions from the 10-K: 209,586 + 33,708 + 28,023 + 35,686 + 109,158 = 416,161 net sales. Cost of sales 220,960 (products 194,116, services 26,844). Operating income 133,050 less other expense, net 321 = pre-tax 132,729 (derived); tax 20,719; net income 112,010. [[10k]] Net income 112,010 → dividends 15,421 + buybacks 90,711 (cash flow statement) + left after payouts 5,878 (112,010 − 15,421 − 90,711, derived). [[10k]]
blocks.period_text: Fiscal-year total ÷ seconds in the fiscal year. Apple's FY2025 was 52 weeks = 364 days = 31,449,600 seconds (not 365 days). Each counter shows that per-second rate × seconds since Jan 1 in your time zone.

blocks.title: Where the cash went, FY2025
blocks.note: Operating cash flow 111,482; capex 12,715; dividends and dividend equivalents 15,421; common stock repurchased 90,711 (cash basis; the 10-K MD&A says $89.3B of shares repurchased, 402 million shares). Apple paid out 7,365 more than it generated: 12,715 + 15,421 + 90,711 − 111,482 = 7,365 (derived), funded from cash, marketable securities and net debt activity. [[10k]]

items: 24.1% a year earlier, which included a State Aid charge [[10k]]

sections.title: Per employee
sections.lede: About 166,000 full-time equivalent employees at fiscal year-end. [[10k]]

items: The 10-K gives headcount only, no pay data [[10k]]

sections.title: Where the money comes from
sections.lede: Apple reports five geographic segments, and sales by product category. It does not disclose revenue by US state.

blocks.title: Net sales by product category, FY2025
Segments, FY2025
blocks.note: Segment operating income excludes R&D ($34.6B) and general & administrative ($8.1B), which are held at corporate. Margins are derived. [[10k]]

blocks.title: By country
blocks.note: Only the US and China are 10% or more of sales, so only they are broken out. Share is derived. [[10k]]

items.title: of gross profit from 26% of revenue
items.text: Services sales were $109.2B (up 14%) with a 75.4% gross margin, against 36.8% for products. That is $82.3B of the $195.2B total gross margin (derived). The 10-K credits advertising, the App Store and cloud services for the growth.

items.title: of stock repurchased in FY2025
items.text: 402 million shares retired. In May 2025 Apple announced a new $100B program and raised the quarterly dividend from $0.25 to $0.26. Cash returned (buybacks 90.7B + dividends 15.4B) was 95% of net income (derived).

items.title: sales fell to $64.4B
items.text: Greater China net sales were $72.6B in FY2023, $67.0B in FY2024 and $64.4B in FY2025, now 15% of the total (derived). The 10-K attributes the FY2025 drop mainly to lower iPhone sales.

items.title: of revenue goes to R&D
items.text: R&D was $34.6B, up 10%, and R&D plus SG&A ($62.2B) was 14.9% of revenue (derived). Cost of sales alone took 53%.

items.title: effective tax rate, versus 24.1% a year earlier
items.text: FY2024's rate included the State Aid Decision charge. The 10-K says the provision fell $10.7B year over year on that item. Cash taxes paid were $43.4B in FY2025.

sections.title: Five years of results
sections.lede: Revenue and net income by fiscal year, from the 10-Ks.

items.text: Revenue $391.0B, net income $93.7B after the State Aid charge. Buybacks $94.9B.
Revenue $416.2B (up 6%), net income $112.0B, a five-year high. Buybacks $90.7B, dividends $15.4B.

sections.title: The short answer
sections.lede: Apple sells devices, and sells services that run on them. In fiscal 2025 Services were **26.2%** of net sales but **42.2%** of gross margin, because Services earned a 75.4% margin against 36.8% on products (derived). [[10k]]

groups.title: Where revenue comes from
groups.sub: Net sales FY2025: products vs. Services.

groups.title: Where gross profit comes from
groups.sub: Gross margin FY2025 as filed. Apple reports operating income only by geography, so gross margin is the product/services profit view.

blocks.callout: Services: **26.2%** of net sales, **42.2%** of gross margin (derived). Gross margin percentage: Services 75.4%, Products 36.8% (as filed).
blocks.note: Apple's 10-K does not allocate R&D (34,550) or SG&A (27,601) to products or Services, so operating profit by product line is not reported and not shown. Reported segment operating income by region is in the Geography section. US$ millions. [[10k]]

sections.title: The flywheel
sections.lede: How Apple's filed numbers connect hardware, Services and what the money is used for. Apple's 10-K does not report active devices or say Services growth comes from its installed base, so this loop shows the filed dollars and the one link the company states itself.

blocks.title: Apple's loop, FY2025

steps.title: Devices sold
steps.text: iPhone 209,586, Mac 33,708, iPad 28,023, Wearables/Home/Accessories 35,686 = 307,003 (derived). Products gross margin was 36.8%.

steps.title: Services on them
steps.text: Services (App Store, advertising, cloud services, AppleCare, payments and more) grew 14%, "primarily due to higher net sales from advertising, the App Store and cloud services". Apple also says it believes "decisions by customers to purchase its hardware products depend in part on the availability of third-party software applications and services".

steps.title: High-margin profit
steps.text: Services gross margin 82,314 of total 195,201 = 42.2% (derived), at 75.4% against 36.8% for products.

steps.title: Reinvest & return
steps.text: R&D 34,550 (+10%). Dividends 15,421 plus buybacks 90,711 returned 106,132 (derived). The 10-K says gross margins "will be subject to volatility and downward pressure".

blocks.note: Buybacks on a cash basis; the MD&A says $89.3B of shares repurchased. [[10k]]
